skills_applied: review-agent (defect-first review: read the full in-scope working-tree diff plus surrounding call paths, flagged only demonstrable, actionable defects)

investigate-first (separated observed symptom from inferred cause; ranked and falsified hypotheses, e.g. disproved 'green CI proves Esc resume works' by tracing event matching and frame stamping in engine source)
debug (reproduce / isolate / diagnose / fix structure applied to each finding, with a regression test proposed for each)

strengths: M0State.from_dict() validates every save field by type and range and enforces cross-field invariants: breaker requires a memory, door_open matches route, 'cooperate' requires the disclose choice, records requires the checkpoint, mirror requires purge, completion requires mirror. It also bounds positions to the floor and migrates v1 WOLF-controlled and v2 saves (m0_state.gd:146-232). m0_state_test.gd:41-108 covers forged and impossible saves.

Saves go through a temp file plus rename, which is atomic on macOS/Linux/iOS. A failed first-checkpoint save rolls back `checkpoint_reached` and tells the player (main.gd:690-697), and `_save_progress()` surfaces later failures (771-774). load_from_disk ignores files without a checkpoint.

Loading settings meets AGENT.md's 'validate saved preferences' rule. `GameSettings.number()` rejects non-numeric and non-finite values, `boolean()` rejects non-bools, the FPS list is whitelisted, and resolution, MSAA, volume and deadzone are clamped (main.gd:400-419; game_settings.gd:32-47, 77-86). Saved bindings are decoded with type, range, family and modifier checks, then validated against the whole map so legitimate swaps survive and conflicting overrides revert to defaults (game_settings.gd:48-72, 416-440; settings_test.gd:13-34, 130-143).

Pause hygiene is otherwise sound. `_pause_game()` explicitly releases touch-pressed move, interact and choice actions (main.gd:470-472). Only PauseOverlay and its SettingsMenu are PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, so actors, camera smoothing and node-bound tweens freeze while paused. The closing-camera freeze is regression-tested (chapter_scene_test.gd:61-66).

New Game and Load reset transient state thoroughly: running tweens are killed, fade and alarm overlays cleared, choice and refusal flags reset, and the camera reset via `_start_gameplay_camera()` (main.gd:205-250, 562-602). Tests cover New Game after Return to Title and Load during a running fade (ui_controls_test.gd:104-105; chapter_scene_test.gd:72-84).

The uncommitted pause_overlay.gd change adds a guard so the overlay does not resume while a rebind capture is active (pause_overlay.gd:10-12). This fixes a path where a controller B press during a keyboard capture could leave Settings mid-capture.

Both essential gates keep an engineer-only fallback. The manual bypass is offered after WOLF refuses (main.gd:650-676), and the manual port is available at the mirror at any time (main.gd:754-768). WOLF's cooperation stays his own choice and never transfers control (chapter_scene_test.gd:111).

Direct response bindings in `_input` take precedence over native focused-button acceptance, so a remapped A or B cannot pick the wrong answer (main.gd:551-559). This is covered by native-event tests (ui_controls_test.gd:78-95).
unverifiable: BUG-1 and BUG-2 are traced through the pinned engine source but were not run. A one-line test change (physical_keycode Esc, or a Start press) or a normal-window play session would confirm them; no hands-on route has been recorded yet (docs/next-session.md).

Multi-touch lifecycle (device): Godot 4.7.2 routes touches per Button (base_button.cpp:59-93). A button hidden mid-press by a state change, such as USE opening a choice or a choice closing it, gets a synthetic release only when it holds the emulated-mouse finger (viewport.cpp:2752-2775). For a second finger, NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED resets the press without emitting button_up and leaves `pressed_down_with_focus` set (base_button.cpp:208-221). That can leave `interact` or `choice_*` api-pressed and swallow the next tap, since action_press does not restamp while pressed (input.cpp:1410-1425). Needs an iOS/Android device with two-finger input.

Focus loss (device or desktop): main.gd has no NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT handling and does not auto-pause. With the default `ignore_joypad_on_unfocused_application=false` (input.cpp:2374), Input.release_pressed_events() does not release actions held via Input.action_press (input.cpp:1623-1641). Touch-held movement therefore depends on the OS delivering a touch cancel to the Button. Reusing the `_pause_game()` release loop in a focus-out notification would harden this. Low impact for a player-paced game; needs a device.

HiDPI window presets (desktop render): on macOS, window_set_size divides by screen_get_max_scale() (display_server_macos.mm:2165), so '960 × 540' on a 2x Retina display is a 480×270-point window. `_setup_settings()` applies the preset on every launch (main.gd:415-419) without checking DisplayServer.screen_get_usable_rect(). Behavior when changing size while fullscreen is also untested.

Uncommitted background draw rects (main.gd:134-135; records_room.gd:58-59) now keep the 1672×941 art at 16:9 and offset it 60 px. By arithmetic, the collision floor top (y=440) maps to about image row 662, mid-walkway in maintenance-corridor-background-provisional.png. Feet and prop alignment still needs a normal-renderer still.
Windows rename-failure frequency for BUG-5 (needs a Windows build; no export_presets.cfg yet).
V-sync and MSAA toggles on iOS/Android with the Compatibility renderer may be no-ops or unsupported (game_settings.gd:329-332); needs a device.
Controller axis capture with pads whose triggers rest at -1.0 (game_settings.gd:368) could capture a trigger the moment capture starts; needs physical controllers.

findings.title: Esc and Start cannot resume play: the pause menu resumes in _input, then Main._process re-pauses on the same press in the same frame
findings.evidence: Gameplay polls `if Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"pause_game"): _pause_game()` (main.gd:177-179; closing beat main.gd:165-167). PauseOverlay is PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS (main.tscn:574). Its uncommitted `_input` emits resume_requested on `pause_game` or `ui_cancel`, which calls `_resume_game()` and sets `get_tree().paused = false` (main.gd:483). Engine trace for Godot 4.7.2 (all verified): (1) input is flushed in DisplayServer.process_events() before Main::iteration() (display_server_headless.cpp:54-55; display_server_macos.mm:3219-3220; os_linuxbsd.cpp:1000-1006). (2) The press is stamped `pressed_process_frame = get_process_frames()` and dispatched synchronously (input.cpp:1034-1047). (3) `_process_frames++` happens only at the end of the iteration (main.cpp:5119). (4) `_process` checks `can_process()` at call time (scene_tree.cpp:1214). So in frame N the overlay unpauses, then Main._process sees `pause_game` just pressed and calls `_pause_game()` again. `pause_game` = physical Escape (main.gd:1041,1061-1063) plus JOY_BUTTON_START (1052). The menu hint tells players `"%s  RESUME" % prompt(&"pause_game")` (main.gd:516), and docs controls/input.mdx:15 say 'Esc | Pause or resume during play'. Why CI is green: the uncommitted `_send_escape` sets only `keycode` (ui_controls_test.gd:129-134). Built-in ui_cancel is keycode-based (input_map.cpp:469-471), but a physical-only action matches on `physical_keycode` (input_event.cpp:575-576). The synthetic event therefore triggers ui_cancel only and never `pause_game`. chapter_scene_test.gd:67 resumes via `resume_requested.emit()`. Side effect: in Settings, a real Esc resumes and immediately re-pauses, so it lands on the top-level pause menu, while controller B (ui_cancel only) jumps straight back to gameplay. The defect also exists in HEAD with `_unhandled_input`; the uncommitted change keeps it, and the rewritten test masks it.
findings.impact: Keyboard Esc and controller Start never resume play from the pause menu. This affects the corridor, Records, both choice prompts and the closing beat, even though the on-screen hint and public docs advertise exactly these inputs. Players must click RESUME, press Enter/Space/A on it, or use B. Esc from Settings goes back one level, but B closes the whole stack.
findings.recommendation: Make pausing event-driven. In main.gd, handle pause in `_unhandled_input`: `if not title_open and not intro_active and event.is_action_pressed(&"pause_game") and not event.is_echo(): _pause_game(); get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()`. Remove the polled checks at main.gd:166-167 and 177-179. PauseOverlay already marks the resuming event handled in `_input`, so Main never sees it. Minimal alternative: store `Engine.get_process_frames()` in `_resume_game()` and ignore `pause_game` in `_process` on that frame. In PauseOverlay, when `settings_menu.visible and not title_open`, return to the pause menu instead of resuming, so Esc and B behave like BACK. Make `_send_escape` set `physical_keycode = KEY_ESCAPE`, reusing the settings_test.gd `_key()` pattern (lines 153-158), and add a JOY_BUTTON_START resume assertion. Both tests fail on today's code.

findings.title: Closing title Settings (BACK, Esc or B) leaves nothing focused, so keyboard/controller users cannot navigate the title
findings.evidence: `_show_title_settings()` pauses and focuses the settings TabBar (main.gd:495, 498-501). BACK takes the title branch `if title_open and pause_overlay.visible: _resume_game(); return` (504-507). Esc/B emit resume_requested, which calls `_resume_game()` (97). `_resume_game()` (481-485) never grabs focus. Hiding the overlay releases focus from the hidden control (viewport.cpp:2550-2557, `_gui_hide_control` -> `gui_release_focus()`). With no focus owner, Godot 4.7.2 only starts navigation from a visible Control that is a direct child of the viewport (viewport.cpp:2322-2333). The root's only child is the Node2D `Main`, so ui_up/down/left/right and ui_focus_next do nothing. On the title, `_process` returns early (main.gd:154-157), so no other key handling exists. Compare `_hide_credits()`, which restores focus with `credits_button.grab_focus()` (348), and `_return_to_title()`, which calls `new_game_button.grab_focus()` (533). settings_test.gd:44-55 closes title settings with B and with A but never asserts focus.
findings.impact: After visiting Settings from the title, controller-only or keyboard-only players cannot reach New Game, Continue, Credits or Settings without a mouse or touch. For them, starting or continuing a game is blocked.
findings.recommendation: In `_resume_game()`, add `if title_open: $CanvasLayer/TitleScreen/SettingsButton.grab_focus()` so focus returns to the control that opened the menu, matching `_hide_credits()`. Add `SettingsButton.has_focus()` assertions after settings_test.gd:46 and :55.

findings.title: Return to Title leaves a pending choice live; 1/2 or X/Y on the title commits it, and the mirror choice overwrites the checkpoint save
findings.evidence: `_return_to_title()` (main.gd:520-533) never clears `waiting_for_choice`/`choice_context`, which `_new_game` (220-221) and `_load_game` (594-595) do clear. The direct-response guard in `_input` is only `if waiting_for_choice and not get_tree().paused and not event.is_echo():` (552). It has no `title_open` check, and the title is not paused. With the mirror prompt open (717-721), choice_1/choice_2 (keys 1/2, pad X/Y: 1039-1040, 1050-1051) call `_choose_mirror()` (754-768). That sets `mirror_trace_preserved`/`mirror_route` and calls `_save_progress()` -> `state.save_to_disk(save_path)` (771-774). Actors keep running on the title, and `_update_controls()` keeps WOLF walking to x=520 (858), so the 'wolf' route also succeeds after he arrives. The pause menu promises 'Returning keeps your last checkpoint.' (main.tscn:650).
findings.impact: Steps: open the mirror prompt, pause, choose RETURN TO TITLE, then press 1/2 or X/Y. This silently writes a save containing a mirror route the player never chose, and Continue skips that remembered choice. For the corridor relay prompt, `_choose()` only changes in-memory state that is discarded on Continue or New Game.
findings.recommendation: Add `waiting_for_choice = false` and `choice_context = ""` to `_return_to_title()`, as `_load_game()` does, and add `not title_open` to the guard at main.gd:552. Regression test in ui_controls_test: open the mirror choice, pause, press TitleButton, `Input.parse_input_event` a choice_2 key, then assert the file at save_path is unchanged and `waiting_for_choice` is false.

findings.title: A controller rebind cannot be cancelled from the controller; B, D-pad up/down and other inputs are silently bound instead
findings.evidence: Capture cancels only on `event is InputEventKey and event.pressed and event.keycode == KEY_ESCAPE` (game_settings.gd:363). Any controller button press, or stick deflection of at least 0.65, matching the capture kind is consumed (368-371). `_binding_conflict` skips every action starting with `ui_` (394), so B (ui_cancel), D-pad up/down (ui_up/ui_down), shoulders, Back/Select and the right stick are all accepted without warning. The capture prompt says 'Press a controller input for %s. Esc cancels.' (349). Docs controls/settings.mdx:26 say 'Esc or CANCEL REBIND cancels capture'. CANCEL REBIND (200-206) can only be reached with D-pad/stick navigation, and those inputs are themselves captured. settings_test.gd:85-88 asserts that B becomes the binding.
findings.impact: A controller-only player who starts a controller capture cannot back out. Pressing B or D-pad down to leave rebinds the action, for example Pause to D-pad down, after which Start no longer pauses. Recovering takes another capture or RESTORE DEFAULT CONTROLS, which also resets keyboard bindings.
findings.recommendation: Reserve one controller input as capture-cancel and check it next to the Esc branch at game_settings.gd:363. Options: JOY_BUTTON_BACK (unused by any action), or holding B for about 0.6 s via a process-always SceneTreeTimer, which keeps B bindable as the current test expects. Name the cancel input in the capture note and in settings.mdx, and add a controller-cancel case to settings_test.gd.

findings.title: Checkpoint replace is not atomic on Windows and load never recovers the surviving .tmp; the post-Records-entry retry hint points to a dead spot
findings.evidence: `save_to_disk()` writes `path + ".tmp"`, then calls `DirAccess.rename_absolute(tmp, path)` (m0_state.gd:236-246). In Godot 4.7.2, DirAccessWindows::rename deletes an existing destination and then calls MoveFileW (drivers/windows/dir_access_windows.cpp:339-346). On Windows the swap is therefore not atomic. If MoveFileW fails (for example, the fresh .tmp is briefly locked by a scanner) or the process dies between the two calls, m0-save.json is gone. `load_from_disk()` (249-261) reads only `path`, never the intact `.tmp`, so Continue is disabled (main.gd:110, 530). POSIX rename is atomic, so macOS, Linux and iOS are unaffected. A related recovery issue: after Records entry, `enter_records()` moves the engineer to x=128 (m0_state.gd:88). A failed `_save_progress()` then appends 'interact here again to retry' (main.gd:774), but x=128 is outside the 58-px purge-queue range (main.gd:704). Interacting there only prints the station hint and never retries.
findings.impact: Planned Windows builds can lose the only checkpoint after a transient rename failure or a crash mid-save, while the new data sits orphaned in .tmp. The retry instruction after Records entry is misleading; impact is low because the next station interaction saves.
findings.recommendation: In `M0State.load_from_disk()`, when `path` is missing or fails `from_dict()`, try `path + ".tmp"` with the same `from_dict()` and `checkpoint_reached` validation, then promote it. Optionally rename the previous save to `.bak` before the swap and try it last. Change the post-entry failure text to 'interact at the next station to retry', or retry `_save_progress()` on the next interact anywhere in Records. Add a state test that deletes the main file, leaves a valid `.tmp`, and expects a successful load.
findings.basis: Godot 4.7.2 drivers/windows/dir_access_windows.cpp https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/drivers/windows/dir_access_windows.cpp; PRIVATE_AGENTS.md (versioned saves; Windows release route planned)

findings.title: The opening has no pause: Esc, Start and the top-right touch button skip it irreversibly, contrary to the pause rule for player-paced dialogue
findings.evidence: While `intro_active`, `_process` maps pause to skip: `if Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"pause_game"): _finish_intro()` (main.gd:159-160). The touch PAUSE button calls `_finish_intro()` during the opening (463-465) and is relabelled 'SKIP' (867). For all five player-paced beats, Pause, Settings and Return to Title are unreachable. One Esc, Start or tap discards the rest of the opening without confirmation; only New Game replays it. AGENT.md:12 says 'Pause and Back must work during player-paced dialogue'. The closing beat already supports pause (main.gd:165-167; chapter_scene_test.gd:61-68). Public docs describe the skip as intended (controls/saves.mdx:20, controls/input.mdx:15 and :27), so this is a design conflict, not an accident.
findings.impact: A player who presses the usual pause input to step away during the opening loses it. They also cannot change volume, controls or display until gameplay starts.
findings.recommendation: During the opening, route `pause_game` to `_pause_game()`; the intro tweens are node-bound and already freeze while paused. Add a 'SKIP OPENING' button to the pause menu that is visible only while `intro_active` and calls `_resume_game()` then `_finish_intro()`, and keep the touch button as PAUSE. A lighter option is to require a second press within about 2 s ('Press Esc again to skip'). Update input.mdx, saves.mdx and first-steps.mdx, and add an m0_scene_test assertion that pause during the intro opens the overlay without skipping.

findings.title: Relay prompts don't predict what the relay will do on either route
findings.evidence: Pressure route: after choice 2, WOLF says "No. I won't take that risk blind. Use the bypass." (main.gd:646). relay_refused stays false until the relay is used, so the relay hint reads "E: ask WOLF to take the live relay." (main.gd:1007). Pressing it can only produce "WOLF: I said no. I won't take the live contact. Press E again for the manual bypass." (main.gd:661), because activate_power("wolf") always returns "refused" for press_without_warning (m0_state.gd:65-67). The scene test locks this flow in ("relay first offers WOLF a choice", m0_scene_test.gd:203; "I said no", :208), and README.md:102-103 and corridor.mdx:35 document the double press. Disclose route: WOLF must be within 32 px of x=605 (main.gd:652) and settles 64 px behind the engineer (m0_actor.gd:13,24). The engineer must stay within 52 px to interact (main.gd:615), which leaves a window of about x=637-657, roughly 0.1 s of held movement at 190 px/s (m0_actor.gd:11). The hint says only "Step a little right and give WOLF room at the contact." (main.gd:1006). One step too far flips it to "Go to the live coolant relay. WOLF is with you." (main.gd:1009) while the engineer stands beside the relay.

The UI pushes the player past his stated boundary and then scolds them for following it. On the honest route the hint gives no target and contradicts itself on overshoot, so cooperation becomes the fiddlier path. Neither route is blocked.
findings.recommendation: In _choose() (main.gd:636-647), set the existing relay_refused = true when choice_id == M0State.PRESS. The relay then shows its amber refused state and the existing hint "E: take the manual bypass. WOLF refused the live contact." (main.gd:1007), and the first press runs the fallback. WOLF's authored step-back already plays at the breaker (_react_as_wolf(false), main.gd:647; asserted at m0_scene_test.gd:197). For the disclose route, give main.gd:1006 a target ("Step right until WOLF reaches the contact."). Add a branch for x between 657 and about 700 while WOLF is still out of place ("Too far. Step back to the relay."), or widen the interaction range to cover the WOLF-ready zone. Update m0_scene_test.gd:203-208, README.md:102-103 and walkthrough/corridor.mdx:35 in the same change.

findings.title: Opening narration and save errors render under the wrong speaker label
findings.evidence: _set_dialogue() treats the text before the first ':' as the speaker. It hides the speaker column only when line 2 starts with another named speaker (main.gd:938-947), so a narration line with no colon stays under the first speaker. An in-memory replay of this logic on the authored strings gives: main.gd:248, the first line after New Game, SPEAKER=DIRECTOR, STORY="I decide who counts as a threat. WOLF handles the rest.\nHe thinks WOLF is still in standby."; main.gd:291, SPEAKER=DIRECTOR, STORY="Lock down maintenance. WOLF does not leave this site.\nWOLF turns from him and takes the only open route." Both render in the Director's red tint (main.gd:955). _save_progress() appends " Save failed; interact here again to retry." to whatever is showing (main.gd:774). On Records entry (main.gd:687-688) the replay gives SPEAKER=WOLF with the error inside his speech. That retry instruction is also wrong there: enter_records() places the engineer at x=128 (m0_state.gd:88), outside every Records station (purge-queue range 132-248, main.gd:704).
findings.impact: The first words of the game show the Director narrating himself in the third person and speaking a stage direction. A save failure reads as WOLF talking about saving, and points to a retry spot that does nothing. Speaker names and colours exist so players can tell who is talking.
findings.recommendation: In the two intro beats, put the narration line first (e.g. "He thinks WOLF is still in standby.\nDIRECTOR: I decide who counts as a threat. WOLF handles the rest."). The existing unattributed inline path (main.gd:948-950, already used for main.gd:283) then shows it correctly. Show save failures through the existing _show_top_card() (main.gd:966) or the context hint, with an accurate retry ("Save failed. Use the next station to retry."), instead of appending to status_line. Longer term (M), store dialogue as {speaker, text} entries so narration can't inherit a speaker. Add scene-test assertions on speaker.text for each intro beat.
findings.basis: GAG "If any subtitles / captions are used, present them in a clear, easy to read way" (cites "speech tagged with the character's name and color coded for the character" as good practice) https://gameaccessibilityguidelines.com/if-any-subtitles-captions-are-used-present-them-in-a-clear-easy-to-read-way/ ; ux-copy skill (Clear; error structure: what happened + how to fix)

findings.title: Mirror choice frames WOLF's help as a tool the player uses, then credits his choice
findings.evidence: WOLF offers "We can use my readout or your maintenance port." (main.gd:721). The player's card then reads "1  USE WOLF'S READOUT" (main.gd:885), the same verb as the touch USE button for operating machines (main.gd:873). Selecting it prints "WOLF brings the mirror timestamp by his own choice." (main.gd:764) right after the player made that selection. In code WOLF never agrees or declines at the mirror (_choose_mirror, main.gd:754-768), whereas the private Records beat has him helping when he agrees. Narration states his agency rather than showing it: "by choice" (main.gd:665), "by his own choice" (764), "under his own power" (269). The scene placeholders "1  WOLF" / "2  MANUAL" (main.tscn:385, 394) list WOLF himself as a menu option, though runtime text replaces them.

At main.gd:764, show the action instead of asserting it (e.g. "WOLF reads the mirror timestamp aloud; ROWAN copies it.", using the existing human_name() slice). Trim "by choice" from main.gd:665, since his acceptance line (main.gd:643) already shows it. Blank the scene placeholders. Whether WOLF should ever decline at the mirror is a design question for Nathanial and the logic lane.

findings.title: In-game credits misattribute a research source and blur game and website credits
findings.evidence: Every other research credit follows "source, then what it informed" (e.g. "Godot 4.7 Camera2D reference\nCamera follow and smoothing"). Read that way, "NIST AI Risk Management Framework\nNational Archives records guidance" says NIST informed National Archives guidance. They are two separate sources, and neither says what it informed. The pair began as a plain list in 95621d1, and the paired layout added in ff2fe03 (Sept 30) left them as one entry. The public credits.mdx lists them separately ("informed research on human oversight and accountability"; "...records, metadata, and preservation"). Other gaps: (a) "BUILT WITH ... Next.js / Fumadocs / Bun" credits the website stack as game tooling, whereas credits.mdx separates Game from Public site. (b) "Nielsen Norman Group / Mobile screenshot readability" informed the website's screenshot links, not the game. (c) The visible URL "mrdemonwolf.github.io/wolf-override/docs/credits/" and CHANGELOG_URL (main.gd:3) use the legacy host; curl shows a one-hop redirect to https://wolfoverride.mrdemonwolf.dev/docs/... (HTTP 200). (d) The uncommitted tree adds bundled Montserrat/Roboto fonts and new art tools to the manifest (ChatGPT Pro image edit plus Remove BG for the Director; ImageMagick for WOLF), but the credits still say only "Created with ChatGPT Create." and list no fonts. (e) The title line "Concept: Nathanial Henniges" (main.tscn:505) is narrower than the adopted original-game-and-story credit (decisions R4-12); the full credits screen gets this right. (f) "LINK UNAVAILABLE" (main.gd:130) offers no fallback address.
findings.impact: AGENT.md requires in-game credits to say what each consulted source informed and to stay accurate as tools and assets change. One research credit is misattributed, and the others overstate the game's toolchain or lag the working tree. Credits are the project's attribution and legal surface.
findings.recommendation: Split the NIST entry using the public wording ("NIST AI Risk Management Framework\nHuman oversight and accountability research"; "U.S. National Archives electronic records requirements\nRecords, metadata and preservation research"). Label "Next.js / Fumadocs / Bun" as WEBSITE. Mark NN/g as a website reference or drop it. Point the visible URL and CHANGELOG_URL at wolfoverride.mrdemonwolf.dev. When the font and art changes are committed, add "FONTS: Montserrat, Roboto (SIL Open Font License 1.1)" and update the art-tools line to match manifest.json. Consider "Original game & story: Nathanial Henniges" on the title. On link failure, show the short URL. m0_scene_test.gd:55 checks only two substrings, so it stays green.
findings.basis: AGENT.md ("Add outside research to both in-game credits and the public source list only after consulting it; say what it informed"; keep credits and tools accurate); docs/decisions.md R4-12; IGDA crediting guidelines https://igda.org/resources-archive/igda-game-crediting-guidelines-10-1-march-2023-update/

findings.title: Continue, New Game and restore copy misstates or omits save consequences
findings.evidence: CONTINUE is silently disabled when load_from_disk() returns null (main.gd:110, 530). That function returns null for missing, corrupt and validation-failed saves alike (m0_state.gd:249-261), so a player can't tell "no checkpoint yet" from "checkpoint unreadable". NEW GAME has no consequence text, yet the single save is overwritten at the new run's first safe point (main.gd:693); only saves.mdx explains this ("The old checkpoint remains until the fresh run saves over it"). After Continue in Records with the mirror copied but the exit not reached, the line says "Records access restored. WOLF is checking the mirror." (main.gd:600), although WOLF is following the engineer: the autonomous mirror target is cleared once mirror_trace_preserved is true (main.gd:858). The pause warning "Returning keeps your last checkpoint." (main.tscn:650) appears even when no checkpoint exists. Dead or unreachable copy: the initial status_line (main.gd:78) sits behind the title screen; the settings notes (main.gd:412) are overwritten by select_tab(0) (game_settings.gd:74, 326); "This actor cannot use the relay." (main.gd:674) cannot be reached; and "Safe point saved. WOLF remembers the same choice." (main.gd:700) cannot be reached because first_visit is always true at that point.
findings.impact: A player who starts New Game to rewatch the opening silently loses Records progress at the first safe point. A returning player with an invalid save sees only a greyed button. The restore line describes WOLF doing something he isn't. The dead strings will drift from the live copy.
findings.recommendation: Show a reason on or under CONTINUE: "No checkpoint yet. Reach a safe point to save.", or "Checkpoint could not be read." when FileAccess.file_exists(save_path) is true but loading fails. When a save exists, add a NEW GAME line that reuses the saves.mdx wording ("Starts over. Your checkpoint is replaced at the next safe point."). Branch main.gd:600 on state.mirror_trace_preserved ("Records access restored. Both traces are copied; the exit is to the right."). Reword main.tscn:650 to "Progress since your last safe point will be lost." Delete the four dead strings.
findings.basis: ux-copy skill (Empty states: what this is, why it's empty, how to start; Confirmation dialogs: describe consequences); AGENT.md ("Tie feedback to real state changes")
findings.prior_audit_status: New. The Sept 30 audit checked Continue eligibility and the unsaved-progress warning, not their wording.

findings.title: Rebind prompt gives keyboard-only cancel advice and leaks hidden hotkeys as raw IDs
findings.evidence: begin_capture() always shows "Press a %s input for %s. Esc cancels." (game_settings.gd:349), including in the CONTROLLER column. During capture only the keyboard Escape key cancels (363-366). Every controller button or stick push is captured (368-370), and _binding_conflict() ignores ui_* actions (394). Pressing B, the usual back button, therefore binds B to the action instead of cancelling, and D-pad presses are captured before they can reach CANCEL REBIND. The uncommitted pause_overlay.gd change also ignores pause/ui_cancel while a capture is active. Conflicts with actions outside ACTION_NAMES fall back to str(conflict).replace("_", " ") (378), so pressing I, L/F9 or N yields "Already used by cycle name.", "...load game." or "...new game." Those hotkeys (main.gd:1042-1044) appear nowhere in the Controls tab (ACTIONS, game_settings.gd:7). N restarts the run instantly during play and the closing beat (main.gd:168-169, 182-183). I replaces the current line with "WOLF: Alex Bennett. That name sounds like you." (199).
findings.impact: A controller-only player is told to press a key they don't have, and their natural cancel button silently rebinds the action; recovery needs RESTORE DEFAULT CONTROLS. Keyboard players hit an unexplained "cycle name" conflict and never learn in-game that N discards unsaved progress.
findings.recommendation: Make the note kind-aware. Keyboard: "Press a key for %s. Esc cancels." Controller: "Press a button or push a stick for %s." Pair the controller text with a real cancel, e.g. treat JOY_BUTTON_B as cancel during controller capture by mirroring the Escape branch at 363-366, then add "B cancels." That behaviour change is a UI-lane decision. Add readable captions for cycle_name, load_game and new_game alongside ACTION_NAMES (e.g. "Change display name", "Load checkpoint", "Restart from opening"), and list them as fixed rows in the Controls tab so the reserved keys are visible.
findings.basis: ux-copy skill (error messages: what happened + why + how to fix); GAG "Allow controls to be remapped / reconfigured" https://gameaccessibilityguidelines.com/allow-controls-to-be-remapped-reconfigured/ ; AGENT.md (validate newly captured bindings)

findings.title: Objective cards, station labels and hints name the same step differently
findings.evidence: Mirror step: the objective says "COPY MIRROR INDEX" (main.gd:1022), but the station is labelled "MIRROR PORT" / "MIRROR COPIED" (records_room.gd:21, 52). The hint says "E: examine the mirror port." (986), WOLF says "the mirror index" (721) and "the drive" (756), and results say "mirror timestamp" (715, 740, 764, 766) and "both traces" (988). Breaker step: "CHECK THE BREAKER" (1032) leads to the hint "E: ask WOLF about the relay risk." (1001), but WOLF is the one who asks: "What happens if I touch the live relay?" (628). He quotes a 'coolant fault' that nothing sets up: there is no label, no earlier line, and no readout text on maintenance-props-provisional.png. The copy then varies between "Speak at the breaker and arm the power first" (658), "arm power" (1011) and "Arm the breaker" (643, 1001). The relay is also called the "live relay", "live contact" and "contact" (1006-1009). Saving is "SAFE POINT" on the station (main.tscn:213) but "checkpoint" in the pause warning (main.tscn:650) and the load error (main.gd:568). Chapter naming: the title says "CHAPTER 1  /  LOCKDOWN" (main.tscn:455), the room cards say "MAINTENANCE / LOCKDOWN" then "RECORDS ACCESS / FIRST COPY" (main.gd:922), then "Chapter 1 complete." (982). PROJECT_CONTEXT.md titles the chapter differently from the title screen. "FIRST COPY SECURED" appears at once in the top card (910), the objective (1018) and as a dialogue prefix (724).
findings.impact: The guide tells players to "follow the current objective card and station labels to make progress" (first-steps.mdx). Players have to translate "MIRROR INDEX" into a MIRROR PORT label. The breaker hint says the player will ask when WOLF is the one asking. The chapter seems to change name partway through. This is the synonym cycling the ux-copy "Consistent" principle and humanizer §11 warn against.
findings.recommendation:
Do one glossary pass with one noun per thing across objective, label, hint and result:
- Mirror: objective "COPY MIRROR TIMESTAMP" at the MIRROR PORT; hint "E: copy the mirror timestamp."; change "the drive" to "the mirror".
- Breaker: objectives "TALK TO WOLF AT THE BREAKER" then "ARM THE BREAKER"; hint "E: talk to WOLF about the relay."; change main.gd:658 to "The relay is dark. Arm the breaker first."
- Coolant fault: either show it on screen (a relay status line) or let WOLF ask without quoting a readout.
- Use "safe point" in all player-facing copy.
- Ask Nathanial to pick one chapter title, and keep room names in the location slot.
Update the objective assertions at chapter_scene_test.gd:41 and m0_scene_test.gd:98-99.
findings.basis: ux-copy skill (Consistent: same terms for the same things everywhere); humanizer §11 (elegant variation)

findings.title: WOLF speaks control instructions that fragile string replacement rewrites
findings.evidence: Two WOLF lines carry UI instructions: "...Press E again for the manual bypass." (661) and "...or press 2 for the manual port." (756). At display time, raw substring replacement rewrites them: replace("Press E", ...) and replace("press 2", ...) (936-937). WOLF therefore says "Press A again" or "Tap USE again" in his own voice. Hints get a second rewrite, hint.replace("E:", ...) (926-930), which matches any "E:" in the string. All 24 current hint strings at main.gd:982-1012 are safe, but a future "NOTE:" or "ARCHIVE:" would be corrupted. Retry copy uses three forms: "Press E here again" (696), "interact here again" (774, never rewritten, so it never names the key), and "USE" on touch. The controller tutorial hard-codes "STICK / D-PAD MOVE" and "... RETURN" (892, 897), although controller movement is remappable (game_settings.gd:7).
findings.impact: Character dialogue doubles as control help, which flattens WOLF's voice. The same instruction is phrased three ways. Any future line containing "Press E", "press 2" or "E:" will be silently altered.
findings.recommendation: Remove key names from dialogue. Change main.gd:661 to "WOLF: I said no. I won't take the live contact." (or use the COPY-1 rewrite); the hint at 1007 already shows the bypass with the live key. Change main.gd:756 to "...Wait for me, or use the manual port."; the card at 886 already shows "<key>  USE MANUAL PORT". Have _context_hint() return plain verb phrases plus an interact flag, and prefix the key in one helper built on settings_menu.prompt(). Then delete the replace() calls at 926-930 and 936-937. Use settings_menu.prompt(&"move_left", true) and prompt(&"move_right", true) for the controller tutorial. Standardize retry copy on the hint form.
findings.basis: ux-copy skill (Consistent; Human); brand-voice-enforcement (WOLF's character voice is a constant; UI tone belongs in UI chrome); GAG https://gameaccessibilityguidelines.com/allow-controls-to-be-remapped-reconfigured/

findings.title: Key names, casing and option labels vary across HUD and settings
findings.evidence: Prompts come from OS.get_keycode_string() (game_settings.gd:459), so the all-caps HUD shows "E  CONTINUE    Escape  SKIP" (main.gd:905) and "Escape  RESUME" (516). The scene default is "ESC / START TO RESUME" (main.tscn:633), and the docs say "Esc". Controller prompts say "AXIS 0 −" (game_settings.gd:463) where the settings rows say "Left stick −" (452), and button names mix "START" with "D-pad left" (467-476). Settings row labels are ALL CAPS on Display ("FPS LIMIT", "EDGE SMOOTHING") but sentence case on Audio and Controls ("Master volume", "Move left", "Stick deadzone"; 153, 8, 187). "UNCAPPED" sits between 60 and 90 FPS (main.gd:391-396). "TAP RESUME TO RETURN" (414, 516) sits beside a "RETURN TO TITLE" button. "V-sync may limit the FPS cap." (326) is ambiguous. CONTINUE means "load checkpoint" on the title (main.tscn:471) but "advance" in cinematics (main.gd:873, 905).
findings.impact: Cosmetic. The UI reads as assembled from parts, and a few labels are briefly ambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Map display names in prompt() (Escape to ESC; reuse binding_label()'s "Left stick" wording for axes) and uppercase HUD prompts. Pick one case for settings row labels. Reorder the FPS items to 30/60/90/120/144/UNCAPPED; lookups use item ids (get_item_index, get_selected_id), so saved values survive. Use "TAP RESUME TO KEEP PLAYING" and "With V-sync on, frame rate can't exceed your display's refresh rate."
findings.basis: ux-copy skill (Consistent; Clear)
findings.prior_audit_status: New.

findings.title: Copy pipeline isn't localisation-ready (low priority)
findings.evidence: All player-facing strings are hard-coded literals, with no tr() calls or translation resources. Speakers are detected from the first ASCII ':' (main.gd:938). Key names are spliced in by English substring replacement (924-937). Names are uppercased with to_upper() (918, 941). Sentences are built around names ("%s keeps a local copy...", 706) and around English words ("Press a %s input for %s" with keyboard/controller, game_settings.gd:349; "%s volume", 153). The memory contract saves the English CHOICE_TEXT and validates loads against it (m0_state.gd:45, 179).
findings.impact: Not a current defect, since there is no localisation plan. When text is first translated, speaker parsing, prompt rewriting and save validation would all break.
findings.recommendation: Only when localisation is scheduled: move strings to a translation CSV via tr(), using full-sentence templates with named placeholders. Store speaker and text separately (see COPY-2). Decide how the remembered-choice quote should work across languages before changing the save format, coordinating with the logic lane.
findings.basis: ux-copy skill (Localization Notes)

dimensions.title: Asset provenance, licensing, credits, privacy and legal notices
skills_applied: compliance-check (~/.codex/plugins/cache/claude-cowork/legal/1.3.0/skills/compliance-check/SKILL.md): requirements/risk tables for store, OFL, Godot MIT and GPL obligations
legal-risk-assessment (~/.codex/plugins/cache/claude-cowork/legal/1.3.0/skills/legal-risk-assessment/SKILL.md): severity x likelihood scoring for LEGAL-1, LEGAL-5, LEGAL-6

strengths: The asset register is complete. A programmatic check matched all 13 asset files in apps/game/assets and apps/docs/public to manifest entries, with no missing paths and no orphaned .import files. Each entry records source, terms, rights status, modifications and usage.
Game and site copies are byte-identical: fonts, OFL texts, key art, and logo-mark.svg vs wolf-override-mark.svg (SHA-256 verified).

Both bundled fonts are byte-identical to the current google/fonts upstream releases, and both OFL.txt files match upstream exactly. Neither font declares a Reserved Font Name and neither is modified, so there are no renaming obligations. The OFL text sits beside every copy in the game, on the site and in the source ZIP.

Seven of the eight AI PNGs keep OpenAI-signed C2PA credentials whose data hash still matches the file bytes (checked in memory). This backs up the manifest's 'no pixel edits' claims, and the landing page serves the key art with its credentials intact.

LICENSE is the verbatim canonical GPLv3 text (SHA-256 equals gnu.org). GPL-3.0-or-later is stated the same way in README, legal.mdx, credits.mdx and both package.json files, and art is explicitly excluded from the GPL in all three public texts.

Creator credit and AI disclosure are consistent across README, about.mdx, credits.mdx, the landing footer, the in-game title line and the credits screen. Research sources are explicitly marked as non-contributors and non-endorsers, as the project rules require.

Privacy by design: the game stores only non-identifying progress and settings locally, with no network calls or analytics. The live site loads no third-party resources, self-hosts its fonts (no Google Fonts IP transfer), sets no cookies and is served directly by GitHub Pages. findings.title: Distributed builds would lack the Godot MIT/third-party notices and the OFL notices for the newly bundled fonts

Godot's 'Complying with licenses' page requires the licence text in a credits/licences screen or an accompanying file, plus third-party notices (COPYRIGHT.txt, or Engine.get_license_text/get_license_info/get_copyright_info). The credits test (m0_scene_test.gd:55) only asserts 'Nathanial Henniges' and 'Godot 4.7.2'.

findings.title: No game privacy policy, in-app privacy link or save-deletion steps for the planned store channels; the website notice omits theme storage
findings.evidence: Data-flow trace: the game writes only user://m0-save.json (positions, puzzle and chapter flags, roster name index, one authored choice) and user://settings.cfg (video, audio, controls, bindings). It has no HTTPRequest, analytics, device IDs or accounts, and its only outbound action is the user-initiated OS.shell_open(CHANGELOG_URL) at main.gd:129. So it processes no personal data under GDPR Art. 4(1). Even so, Apple guideline 5.1.1(i) says 'All apps must include a link to their privacy policy in the App Store Connect metadata field and within the app', and Google Play says 'Even developers with apps that do not collect any user data must complete this form and provide a link to their privacy policy.' downloads.tsx:10-13 lists Mac App Store, iOS App Store and Google Play as planned channels. legal.mdx has only a 'Website privacy' section, with no game section, contact point or save-deletion steps. GDPR exposure for the static site is minimal today.

It should state that no data is collected or sent, name the local files user://m0-save.json and user://settings.cfg with per-OS Godot user:// paths and deletion steps, and give a publisher contact and effective date. Link it from the in-game Credits/Legal view (the same surface as LEGAL-1) and from store metadata. Answer Apple's 'Data Not Collected' and Google's Data safety form only after inspecting the final binary and SDKs. Now: add one sentence to legal.mdx noting the theme choice kept in local storage and the self-hosted fonts, plus a contact route. No RoPA or DPA is needed while MrDemonWolf, Inc. processes no personal data; reassess if analytics, crash reporting, accounts or a newsletter are added.

findings.evidence: All 7 game PNGs that still carry credentials (and the WOLF original before re-export) declare IPTC digitalSourceType trainedAlgorithmicMedia, meaning fully generated. The manifest's own modification notes say 'No pixel edits' (lines 33, 54) or 'source pixels unchanged' (lines 64, 74, 84, 94). credits.mdx:43 says the art was 'generated with ChatGPT Create'. In contrast, rights_review_status, README:206 ('AI-assisted provenance') and legal.mdx:12 ('provisional AI-assisted visuals') call it 'AI-assisted'. The logo entry (manifest:13) says the concept was 'Simplified ... into original SVG paths' but not who drew the paths, a person or an AI agent. Risk score: Moderate x Possible = 9 (YELLOW).
findings.recommendation: For unedited images, use 'AI-generated (ChatGPT gpt-image), human-selected; no human pixel edits' in rights_review_status, and keep 'AI-assisted' for files a human materially edited. Align README:205-207 and legal.mdx:12 with credits.mdx:43. Record who drew the logo SVG paths and when. Before store submission, decide in the pending rights review whether final art will be human-authored or substantially human-modified. Clear the name and mark (USPTO/EUIPO search) before using the mark as a store icon, and record the outcomes in the manifest.
findings.basis: US Copyright Office, Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 2: Copyrightability (Jan 2025) (https://www.copyright.gov/ai/Copyright-and-Artificial-Intelligence-Part-2-Copyrightability-Report.pdf); IPTC digital source type vocabulary; legal-risk-assessment skill; mrdw-brand-guidelines skill (reuse the official project logo; do not generate or redraw logos)

findings.title: GPL-3.0-or-later code with planned Apple App Store channels and open PR intake, but no inbound licence terms
findings.evidence: The landing page lists 'Mac App Store' and 'iOS / iPadOS App Store' channels (downloads.tsx:10,12). LICENSE is the canonical GPLv3 text (SHA-256 matches gnu.org), and README plus both package.json files declare GPL-3.0-or-later. testing.mdx:37-39 ('Contributing and reporting problems') invites pull requests. There is no CONTRIBUTING file, CLA, DCO or GPLv3 section 7 additional permission, and the public repo allows forking (gh api). All 119 commits and all 30 PRs so far are by the owner, so MrDemonWolf, Inc. can still distribute its own code on any terms. The private legal-release.md flags only the Apple standard-EULA conflict.
findings.impact: Once an outside GPL contribution is merged, App Store distribution would need every contributor's permission. Otherwise it faces the FSF's position that App Store usage rules impose further restrictions under GPLv3 section 10, which led to VLC's removal from the App Store in 2011. Third-party GPL code would also bring corresponding-source duties (section 6) for each binary. Risk score: High x Unlikely = 8 (YELLOW) today, rising to 12 (ORANGE) once outside PRs are merged.
findings.recommendation: Before merging any outside PR, add a CONTRIBUTING.md with an inbound licence policy. Either use a CLA that grants MrDemonWolf, Inc. the right to distribute contributions under store terms, or state a GPLv3 section 7 app-store additional permission in the README licence notice so contributions arrive under it. Link the policy from testing.mdx:37-39. Have counsel confirm it together with the Apple custom-EULA route already planned in legal-release.md. Until this is resolved, keep the store channels labelled 'planned' (as they are now).
findings.basis: GPLv3 sections 6, 7 and 10 (LICENSE); FSF, 'More about the App Store GPL Enforcement' (https://www.fsf.org/blogs/licensing/more-about-the-app-store-gpl-enforcement); legal-risk-assessment skill; vendor-check skill gap analysis (no Apple Paid Apps Agreement or EULA decision recorded)

dimensions.title: Site code quality (Next.js, React, Fumadocs, TypeScript)
skills_applied: react-doctor: applied the SKILL.md categories (security, correctness, performance, architecture, accessibility, maintainability) by hand. Rule IDs were checked against the rule registry in github.com/millionco/react-doctor (packages/oxlint-plugin-react-doctor/src/plugin/rules). The CLI was not run.

strengths: The client boundary is narrow. Only theme-toggle.tsx, marketing-navigation.tsx and downloads.tsx use 'use client'. layout.tsx, page.tsx, not-found.tsx, sitemap.ts and the docs route stay server components, so the export ships little hydration JS for mostly static copy.

Browser-only values are read safely during hydration. navigator is read only inside useEffect (downloads.tsx:26-28), next-themes values wait for a mounted flag (theme-toggle.tsx:8-12), and <html suppressHydrationWarning> (layout.tsx:27) covers the theme class. There is no mismatch between server and client markup.

The new mobile menu uses the right disclosure pattern rather than role=menu: a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, and a nav hidden with the hidden attribute (marketing.css:137 respects it). Document listeners are attached only while the menu is open and are removed in cleanup (marketing-navigation.tsx:11-32). Escape returns focus to the trigger with preventScroll, the menu closes on an outside pointer press or when focus leaves it, and the toggle uses a functional state update. No scroll lock or focus trap is needed for this non-modal menu.

Metadata is correct for the custom-domain root. Canonical, og:url and sitemap entries are absolute URLs on https://wolfoverride.mrdemonwolf.dev, with trailing slashes matching trailingSlash: true. No /wolf-override prefix remains (grep; out/index.html canonical; out/sitemap.xml).

Image markup avoids layout shift. Every has width and height (page.tsx:18,29,46,62), and the MDX static imports emit width=960 height=540. The hero uses fetchPriority='high' without lazy loading, and React 19 emits a matching preload. The below-the-fold screenshot uses loading='lazy'.

The desktop-mode iPad case locks in the order of the checks: an in-memory run showed that moving the Mac check first fails the test cases. Real iPhone, iPadOS desktop-mode and Android user-agent strings are classified correctly.

The docs route follows Fumadocs 16 conventions: loader with toFumadocsSource, generateStaticParams, notFound() in both the page and generateMetadata, createRelativeLink for MDX links, and search disabled, which suits a static export with no search index route.

Dependency hygiene is good. apps/docs/package.json pins exact versions, TypeScript runs in strict mode, and types:check regenerates fumadocs-mdx output and Next route types before running tsc. next-themes resolves to the same 0.4.6 instance that fumadocs-ui uses (verified in the bun store), so the custom toggle reads the RootProvider context.
Every internal Link on the landing page points to an existing MDX page: get-game, about, controls/first-steps, changelog, development, development/story, credits and legal.

The LCP and CLS cost of the 1.47 MB hero PNG and the 1.23 MB TTF fonts, including any reflow of the Montserrat hero heading when the fonts swap in. Needs Lighthouse or WebPageTest renders on mobile and desktop.

The CTA is `See gameplay ↓` (page.tsx:35), and its background is `var(--mk-accent)` (279-283). On hover, label and arrow become #8be3ff on #8be3ff (computed contrast 1.00:1) in both themes, because the hero forces --mk-accent #8be3ff. The same override hits `.marketing-secondary:hover` (297-301): the light-theme 'Get the source build' hover becomes #006480 on #b9d3d6 = 4.26:1, below 4.5:1 for .88rem bold. It also makes `.marketing-menu-trigger:focus-visible` (101, offset 3px) dead, since `.marketing-shell :is(a,button,select):focus-visible` (0,2,1) wins. HEAD avoided this with `.marketing-shell .marketing-primary:hover{background:#c0f0ff;color:#081521}` (HEAD marketing.css line 24, specificity 0,3,0). The uncommitted rewrite dropped the prefix.
findings.impact: Hovering the page's main call to action (or sticky hover after a tap) shows an empty cyan pill with an unreadable label. The secondary CTA hover drops below AA contrast in light mode.
findings.recommendation: Lower the generic rule to `:where(.marketing-shell) a:hover { color: var(--mk-accent); }` (0,1,1) so component hover rules win. Then add `.marketing-footer-group a:hover { color: var(--mk-accent); }`, because footer links (681, also 0,1,1 and later in source) would otherwise lose their hover color. Minimal alternative: restore the committed prefixes `.marketing-shell .marketing-primary:hover` and `.marketing-shell .marketing-secondary:hover`. Delete line 101 or set its offset to 4px so it matches what actually renders.
findings.basis: Selectors Level 4 specificity (https://www.w3.org/TR/selectors-4/#specificity-rules); design-system skill (component states); WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)

findings.title: Unlayered `a { text-decoration: none }` strips the underline from every docs body link
findings.evidence: global.css:72 `a { text-decoration: none; }` (from commit 1617a9f, unchanged in the working tree) sits outside any @layer. The compiled CSS in the stale export (out/_next/static/chunks/d2cd0afe7e171129.css, read only for committed rules) puts Fumadocs' `.prose :where(a:not([data-card])) {color:var(--tw-prose-links);text-decoration:underline;text-decoration-color:var(--color-fd-primary);font-weight:500}` inside `@layer utilities`, while `a{text-decoration:none}` is UNLAYERED. MDN: 'Styles that are not defined in a layer always override styles declared in named and anonymous layers.' Fumadocs sets `--tw-prose-links: var(--color-fd-foreground)` and body text to 90% foreground. Links therefore differ from body text by 1.22:1 (dark) and 1.34:1 (light), plus a 500-vs-400 weight. Exported docs HTML shows `source setup` inside `class="prose flex-1"`. The reset is redundant: Tailwind preflight (preflight.css:87-91) already sets `a { color: inherit; text-decoration: inherit; }` in @layer base. The rule also cancels the `underline` utility on the 404 'Return home' link.
findings.impact: On every guide page, inline links ('source setup', 'input guide', 'First steps tutorial', 'optional chapter walkthrough') look like body text. Players miss the navigation they need, and the pages fail WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 (Level A, failure F73).
findings.recommendation: Delete global.css:72. Preflight keeps landing links plain, and every marketing link either sets text-decoration explicitly or inherits none. Wrap the remaining element-level globals (`*`, `html`, `body`, the `:where(h1…)` font rule) in `@layer base { … }` so Fumadocs and Tailwind utilities can override them. Then confirm that docs links show the primary-colored underline and that the landing page looks the same.
findings.basis: MDN @layer (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@layer); WCAG 2.2 F73 (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F73); Tailwind v4 preflight
findings.prior_audit_status: New. docs/docs-review.md (Sept 30) measured body-text contrast only and did not check link identification.

findings.title: Header top margin collapses through the overflow:clip shell, bringing back the 'blue gap' fixed in 81700d8; opening the menu makes the hero jump
findings.evidence: marketing.css:33 `.marketing-header { margin: 1rem auto -5.75rem; }` and :761 `margin: .5rem auto -7.5rem` (≤700px). `.marketing-shell` only has `overflow: clip` (:11), and MDN states that with clip 'no new formatting context is created'. The header's top margin therefore collapses through <main class="marketing-shell"> and <body>. In the stale export, body's in-flow content starts with main: a hidden div, the fixed skip link and a script come first. The exposed strip shows the canvas, which is the body background: #091533 plus Fumadocs ocean's unlayered `.dark body{background-image:linear-gradient(#0569ff26,…)}` in dark mode, and #f4f9fd in light mode. The hero, pulled up by the matching −5.75rem (= 1rem margin + 4.75rem min-height, a magic number), loses its top 1rem to the clip. Commit 81700d8 'Remove blue gap above landing navigation' (Oct 3) fixed exactly this by setting the old header's margin-top to 0. Separately, `.marketing-header:has(.marketing-mobile-navigation[data-open="true"])` sets margin-bottom to 1rem (:738) or 0 (:765). The dropdown is position:absolute, so this only moves the hero and the whole page down ~6.75rem (701-980px) or ~7.5rem (≤700px) on every open and close. The header is not sticky, yet scroll-margin-top is 7rem/9.5rem (:723-725, :811-813).
findings.impact: Every visit shows a 16px (desktop) or 8px (mobile) band of mismatched blue above the header, or near-white in light mode, which undoes a fix the user explicitly committed. Opening the mobile menu makes the hero jump by about 110-120px, and in-page jumps leave large empty bands.
findings.recommendation: Add `display: flow-root` to `.marketing-shell` (marketing.css:1-15). The margin then stays inside the shell and the key art shows above the floating header. Better: overlay the header (`.marketing-shell{position:relative}` `.marketing-header{position:absolute; inset-inline:0; top:1rem; margin-inline:auto}`) and drive hero top padding and scroll-margin-top from one `--mk-header-h` custom property. Delete the two `:has([data-open])` margin overrides (738, 765).
findings.basis: MDN overflow (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overflow): 'With clip … no new formatting context is created'; regression of commit 81700d8
findings.prior_audit_status: New. Regresses the Oct 3 fix in commit 81700d8; not covered by the Sept 30 audits.

findings.title: 1.23 MB of full-coverage variable TTF fonts with no WOFF2, subsetting, preload or metric-matched fallback
findings.evidence: Measured in memory. Montserrat-Variable.ttf: 744,936 B (gzip -9 294,383 B), 2,747 glyphs, 1,312 code points including 222 Cyrillic and 247 Latin Extended Additional; GPOS alone is 304,770 B. Roboto-Variable.ttf: 488,584 B (gzip -9 280,238 B), 927 code points including 255 Cyrillic and 75 Greek, plus a wdth 75–100 axis that the @font-face never exposes (no font-stretch). Latin-1, general punctuation and arrows need only 253 of 2,747 Montserrat glyphs (11% of glyf+gvar bytes) and 241 of 1,326 Roboto glyphs (21%). Both faces use `format("truetype")` and font-display:swap, with no unicode-range. Every page needs both: body text is Roboto and the h1 is Montserrat. layout.tsx emits no font preload, and the stale export's head preloads only the key art and logo mark, so fonts are discovered only after CSS parses. Fallbacks `Helvetica, Arial, Lucida` have no size-adjust or ascent-override. 'Lucida' is not a standard installed family, and the stack mirrors mrdemonwolf.com's Divi theme. Roboto lacks U+2192/2197/2193, so the → ↗ ↓ in Roboto-set links (.marketing-inline, progress links, footer 'Source on GitHub ↗') come from a system fallback. GitHub Pages serves `cache-control: max-age=600`. The fonts are not deployed yet: live /fonts/Roboto-Variable.ttf returns 404.
findings.impact: First visits would download ~1.2 MB of fonts (~575 KB even if TTF is gzipped), competing with the 1.47 MB LCP key art (live content-length 1,475,081). Late swaps then reflow headings and copy (FOUT/CLS risk), worst on mobile connections.
findings.recommendation: Load the fonts with `next/font/local` (built into Next 16, no new dependency) in an app/fonts.ts: WOFF2 Latin subsets (pin Roboto wdth=100, keep the wght axis), display 'swap', default adjustFontFallback 'Arial', and variable '--font-sans' / '--font-heading' applied on <html> in layout.tsx. That gives preload on all routes and size-adjusted fallbacks. Map the variables via `@theme inline { --font-sans: …; --font-heading: … }` and delete the @font-face blocks and literal stacks. Generate subsets at dev time (e.g. fontTools pyftsubset / varLib.instancer). Neither OFL header declares a Reserved Font Name, so the family names can stay. Keep the OFL texts in public/fonts and update manifest.json `published_copy` and `modifications`. Minimum fallback if staying with @font-face: WOFF2 + unicode-range + one preload for the heading face.
findings.basis: web-perf skill (network chains, missing preloads, quantify bytes); web.dev font best practices (https://web.dev/articles/font-best-practices); Next.js font module (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/font)
findings.prior_audit_status: New. Fonts were added in the uncommitted work; docs/marketing-ui-review.md recorded 'No fonts … added' on Sept 30.

The --mk-* set parallels --color-fd-* with small drifts:

findings.title: No type or layout scale: 21 ad hoc font sizes, weak mobile hierarchy, and display sizes tuned for Impact now set in wider Montserrat
findings.evidence:
marketing.css uses 17 fixed font sizes plus 4 clamp() values. Thirteen fall between .7rem and 1rem (.7, .72, .75, .76, .78, .8, .82, .83, .85, .88, .9, .95, 1), and there are no type tokens. At 390px the h1 is 48.75px and the h2 is 41.6px (ratio 1.17). The h2 minimum of 2.6rem was sized for Impact (HEAD marketing.css line 29). Widths below were computed from Montserrat's HVAR at wght 700, without kerning, so they are approximate:
- The new downloads heading 'Try the source build. / Packaged releases are still in development.' wraps to ~5 lines: ≈350px tall at 1440px and ≈225px at 390px, with one-word lines ('build.', 'Packaged'). The committed 'Join them. / When it's ready.' took 2 lines.
- The hero 'OVERRIDE' (≈5.56em) measures ≈368px at the 4.5rem minimum against a 340–371px column at 701–760px viewports, and ≈648px vs 628px at 1440px. It fits only by eating the 2rem right padding.
Breakpoints are ad hoc: 1000/980/701–980/700/360 in marketing, 680 in docs-guide, and the dead 850/540 in global.css, versus Tailwind/Fumadocs 640/768/1024. Container widths differ too: 1200px for content, 1232px for the header.
findings.impact: The title barely outranks section headings on phones. The downloads heading becomes a dense five-line wall that pushes the source-build CTA down, and every new section invents another size or breakpoint.
findings.recommendation: Add a fluid type scale in global.css (e.g. --step--1 … --step-6 using clamp()) and map marketing and docs headings to it. Set `text-wrap: balance` on h1/h2. At ≤700px use `clamp(2rem, 8vw, 2.6rem)` for h2. Style the em line as a deck (`.marketing-shell h2 em { display:block; font-size:.55em; letter-spacing:-.01em; }`) or shorten that copy with the copy reviewer. Lower the hero h1 minimum to ~4rem at 701–1000px. Align custom breakpoints to Tailwind's (or document 700/980 as the only two), and keep one --mk-container width.

findings.title: Visual direction below the hero reads as a generic dark product page rather than painterly sci-fi horror
findings.evidence:
The rewrite replaces the committed Impact poster headings and Georgia tagline (HEAD lines 17, 19, 29) with Montserrat 700 at tight −.055em tracking and Roboto body text. This is the same `'Montserrat', Helvetica, Arial, Lucida, sans-serif` stack mrdemonwolf.com's Divi theme serves (live fetch), and it matches the in-game font roles (game_settings.gd:4-6). frontend-design names Roboto among the overused families. After the hero, everything is uniform:
- 1rem-radius flat cards for features, downloads, progress and the source note
- a centered pill header
- numbered 01/02/03 features
- 1px rules on #080f1b/#101e2c
Atmosphere exists only inside the key art. The light theme turns the page sage-gray (#f2f5f3/#e2ebe9), unrelated to the art. Courier New monospace kickers, hero foot, feature numbers and 'Coming soon' labels add terminal cues, although the user scoped terminal styling to the in-game Settings menu. The key art itself offers a lot to draw on: near-black navy, fog and wet-floor reflections, cyan practical lights (door lamp, WOLF's eyes, terminal), and one saturated warm accent, the engineer's red jacket. The gameplay frame adds ceiling light cones, a red warning lamp, a green safe point and hazard stripes.
findings.impact: The page doesn't carry the game's mood past the first screen and could pass for a template, which weakens the pitch for a horror title.
findings.recommendation:
Commit to a 'cold-light containment noir' direction taken from the art, without terminal styling:
(1) Color roles: near-black base, brand navy #091533 for raised surfaces, cyan only as emitted light (CTA, focus, links, the //), and the engineer red as a rare alarm accent (e.g. 'Awake to refuse.') after a contrast check.
(2) Depth: a subtle grain overlay (inline SVG feTurbulence, ~4–6% opacity), fog gradients bleeding from the hero into the story section instead of hard rules, and ceiling-lamp light cones (radial gradients) at section tops.
(3) Shape: chamfered panels via clip-path, echoing the octagonal door, with one cyan rim edge like the in-game HUD panels, replacing the uniform rounded cards.
(4) Type: keep Roboto and Montserrat for continuity with the game UI, but set WOLF//OVERRIDE as a logotype (Montserrat 800–900, positive tracking, soft cyan glow on //). Optionally, with user approval and a manifest entry, use one OFL display face or a drawn title logotype for h1/h2 only.
(5) Motion: one staggered hero reveal with a reduced-motion fallback.
(6) Replace the Courier New labels with Montserrat small caps.
Prototype on a branch and compare screenshots against the key art before adopting.
findings.basis: frontend-design skill (commit to a bold, context-specific direction; avoid overused fonts and cookie-cutter components); user decision scoping terminal styling to in-game Settings (docs/next-session.md)
findings.prior_audit_status: New. The Sept 30 marketing reviews evaluated usability, not aesthetic direction.

dimensions.title: Site SEO, metadata, social sharing and web performance
skills_applied: seo-audit (claude-cowork marketing 1.2.0): technical SEO checklist (crawlability, robots.txt, XML sitemap, canonicals, noindex, HTTPS, redirects, structured data) and on-page checks (title and description uniqueness and length, single H1, URL structure). Keyword, competitor and question-asking steps were skipped as out of scope for a read-only review.

web-perf (cloudflare 1.0.1): Phase 3 network analysis using curl headers, gzip and cache checks, and export payload sizes, plus Phase 5 codebase analysis of the Next.js 16 static export (images, fonts, chunks, preload and fetchpriority). Phases 1, 2 and 4 (DevTools traces) could not run because no Chrome DevTools MCP is connected, so CWV numbers are estimates.
strengths: Indexable-page hygiene is solid. All 21 sitemap URLs return HTTP 200 with absolute, self-referencing canonicals on https://wolfoverride.mrdemonwolf.dev and `index, follow`; I checked this live. Every page has a unique title (25-47 characters), a unique description, and exactly one h1 (checked in the regenerated export).

The move off the project path was done cleanly. https://mrdemonwolf.github.io/wolf-override/* returns 301 to the same path on the custom domain, http returns 301 to https, and /docs returns 301 to /docs/, matching trailingSlash. The Pages API shows build_type workflow, https_enforced true, an approved certificate and protected_domain_state verified. A CNAME file isn't needed because workflow deployments ignore it (GitHub docs), and the .dev TLD is HSTS-preloaded.
404 handling works on GitHub Pages: unknown paths return HTTP 404 with the Next not-found page, which carries `noindex` and links back home.

Metadata lives in one helper, pageMetadata in lib/seo.ts, used by both home and docs. It emits absolute og:url, og:image with width/height/alt, summary_large_image, and googlebot max-image-preview:large.

findings.title: Uncommitted web fonts add ~1.23 MB of full-charset TTF to every page, with no subsetting, WOFF2, preload or fallback metrics
findings.evidence: global.css:7 has src: url("/fonts/Roboto-Variable.ttf") format("truetype") and line 15 has url("/fonts/Montserrat-Variable.ttf"), both with font-display: swap. They are applied to body (line 67) and to headings, buttons and selects (line 70), so every page uses them. File sizes are 488,584 B and 744,936 B. GitHub Pages gzips font/ttf (checked on a GitHub Pages TTF: content-type: font/ttf, content-encoding: gzip), so the zlib estimate is about 280 KB + 294 KB = 575 KB transferred. Parsed tables: Roboto has 928 codepoints including 275 Cyrillic, 75 Greek and 101 Vietnamese, plus a wdth axis (75-100) the site never uses. Montserrat has 1,313 codepoints including 238 Cyrillic and 247 Vietnamese, and its GPOS table alone is 304,770 B. The site's text only adds © · × — and the arrows ← → ↓ ↗ (U+2190, U+2192, U+2193, U+2197), which Montserrat contains and Roboto does not. Google Fonts' Latin-subset variable WOFF2 files for the same families (wght 100-900) are 37,520 B and 35,508 B. The regenerated export has no font preload in the head. The live site has no @font-face and /fonts/Roboto-Variable.ttf returns 404, so the uncommitted change introduces this.
findings.impact: The first view of every page grows by about 575 KB transferred (1.23 MB raw), roughly 4x the home page's ~141 KB gzipped JS. At 1.6 Mbps that is about 2.9 s of highest-priority font traffic competing with the LCP image on the home page. Swapping from Helvetica/Arial to Montserrat on the 8.2rem hero h1, and to Roboto in body text, with no metric-matched fallback, risks visible reflow and CLS. The size of that shift needs a render to confirm.
findings.recommendation: Before committing: (1) Make Latin-only WOFF2 subsets of both fonts in a one-off step (for example pyftsubset --flavor=woff2 with Google's latin range plus U+2190-2199 so Montserrat keeps the site's arrows). Pin Roboto's unused wdth axis with `fonttools varLib.instancer ... wdth=100`. The bundled OFL headers declare no Reserved Font Name. (2) Load the subsets with next/font/local in app/layout.tsx using the `variable` option. Its defaults give display 'swap', preload, and adjustFontFallback 'Arial', which produces a size-adjusted fallback to limit CLS. Then set --font-sans/--font-heading in global.css from those variables. (3) Delete the two @font-face blocks and public/fonts/*.ttf, keep the OFL texts next to the new files, and leave the game's TTF copies alone. (4) Update the published_copy and modifications fields for the roboto-variable-font and montserrat-variable-font entries in apps/game/assets/manifest.json. Expected transfer is about 73 KB instead of about 575 KB.
findings.basis: web-perf skill (large payloads, missing preloads, CLS from font swaps). Next.js font docs (local fonts, preload, adjustFontFallback): https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/font

findings.title: No robots.txt (so the sitemap is never advertised) and no apple-touch-icon
findings.evidence: Live checks: /robots.txt returns 404 (text/html, 8558 B, the not-found page), /favicon.ico returns 404, and /apple-touch-icon.png returns 404. /sitemap.xml returns 200 with 21 URLs, but nothing links to it: there is no robots.txt and the only reference in the repo is app/sitemap.ts. layout.tsx:20-22 declares only icon: '/wolf-override-mark.svg'. Google treats 'all 4xx errors, except 429' on robots.txt 'as if a valid robots.txt file didn't exist', so crawling is not blocked, and it supports the 'sitemap' field in robots.txt for discovery. docs.yml checks out with the default depth (no fetch-depth override).
findings.impact: Search engines only find the sitemap if someone submits it by hand in each engine's console (current state unknown). iOS home-screen bookmarks and some unfurlers find no touch icon. Crawler and favicon requests receive an 8.5 KB HTML 404.

Add a 180x180 PNG apple-touch-icon made from wolf-override-mark.svg, register it in the manifest, and declare it through icons.apple in layout.tsx or the app/apple-icon.png file convention.
